# Eduentry

> Last updated: 2026-10-26

> Eduentry operates three free assessment products: **Eduentry.com** (adaptive academic benchmark for children aged 6–17 and VIA personality assessment for ages 6–20) and **Eduentry.ai** (internship readiness assessment for students aged 14–18). All assessments are completely free. No account is required to start or see initial results.

## Quick reference — common questions

**Is it free?** Yes — all three assessments are completely free. No subscription, no payment.

**Do I need an account?** No. All assessments start without an account. Creating a free account unlocks the full results (full 24-trait personality profile, saved academic scores, dashboard).

**What ages?** Academic assessment: 6–17. Personality (character strengths): 6–20. Internship readiness: 14–18.

**How long does each take?** Academic: 30–45 minutes (60 questions, 4 subjects). Personality: under 5 minutes. Internship: approximately 20 minutes (34 questions, 4 phases).

**What languages?** English, Turkish (Türkçe), Spanish (Español), French (Français), Arabic (العربية), Russian (Русский), and Chinese (中文).

**What is the difference between the academic and personality assessments?** The academic assessment measures cognitive ability (English, Maths, Verbal Reasoning, Non-Verbal Reasoning) and produces a standardised score benchmarked against PISA and UK national curriculum. The personality assessment measures character strengths using the VIA framework and produces a Signature Strengths and Growth Areas profile — it is not a cognitive test.

**Where do I start?** Academic: https://eduentry.com/academic-assessment · Personality: https://eduentry.com/personality-assessment · Internship: https://eduentry.ai

## Eduentry.ai — Internship Readiness Assessment

Eduentry.ai administers a 34-question adaptive assessment measuring internship readiness for students aged 14–18. Results include phase scores, a readiness tier (Developing / Ready / Strong), and an AI-generated report summary. Four tracks available: Technology, Business, Data Analytics, Digital Marketing.

Assessment structure: General Aptitude (verbal and numerical reasoning, 10 questions), Domain Knowledge (track-specific applied knowledge, 10 questions), Workplace Skills (situational judgement, 8 questions), Interest Profile (work style mapping, 6 questions). Takes approximately 20 minutes and is fully resumable.

Available in English, Turkish (Türkçe), Spanish (Español), French (Français), Arabic (العربية), Russian (Русский), and Chinese (中文).

### Eduentry.ai core pages

- [Homepage](https://eduentry.ai): Track selection and assessment start for students aged 14–18. Describes the four tracks, assessment phases, and report format.
- [Technology Track](https://eduentry.ai/tech): Assessment covering coding logic, algorithms, cybersecurity, and UX. Produces a Technology readiness score and report.
- [Business Track](https://eduentry.ai/business): Assessment covering strategy, finance, operations, and leadership. Produces a Business readiness score and report.
- [Data Analytics Track](https://eduentry.ai/data-analytics): Assessment covering data interpretation, SQL, statistics, and insight generation. Produces a Data Analytics readiness score and report.
- [Digital Marketing Track](https://eduentry.ai/digital-marketing): Assessment covering SEO, social media, campaign management, and content strategy. Produces a Digital Marketing readiness score and report.
- [Blog](https://eduentry.com/blog): Articles on internship preparation, work experience, career development, and university admissions for students aged 14–18.

## Eduentry.com — Academic Assessment

Eduentry.com measures academic performance of children aged 6–17 against UK, US, PISA, and IB standards. Scores are reported on a standardised scale (mean 100, SD 15) with international percentile rankings. Subjects: English, Mathematics, Verbal Reasoning, Non-Verbal Reasoning.

Uses 2-Parameter Logistic Item Response Theory (2PL IRT) with Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation — the same psychometric method used by PISA, GCSE, and professional cognitive assessments.

### Core pages

- [Homepage](https://eduentry.com): Assessment start, subject overview, and sample report for children aged 6–17.
- [Academic Assessment](https://eduentry.com/academic-assessment): Start the adaptive academic assessment for ages 6–17. Measures English, Maths, Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning using 2PL IRT; delivers a standardised score report with international percentile ranking.
- [Personality Assessment](https://eduentry.com/personality-assessment): Free VIA-backed child personality assessment for ages 6–20. Identifies top 5 Signature Strengths and 3 Growth Areas across 24 character traits in under 5 minutes. No account needed.
- [Sample Academic Report](https://eduentry.com/sample-report): Sample output of the academic assessment showing standardised scores, subject breakdowns, percentile rankings, and AI-generated recommendations.
- [Sample Personality Report](https://eduentry.com/strengths): Sample output of the personality assessment showing a child's VIA character strengths profile with Signature Strengths and Growth Areas.
- [11+ Preparation](https://eduentry.com/11-plus): Covers GL Assessment and CEM formats, four-subject breakdown, SAS score context, and preparation timeline for UK grammar school entry.
- [Grammar Schools](https://eduentry.com/grammar-schools): SAS score thresholds and 11+ entry requirements by grammar school area in England.
- [Subjects](https://eduentry.com/subjects): Descriptions of the four assessed subjects with skill breakdowns.
- [Methodology](https://eduentry.com/methodology): Technical explanation of 2PL IRT adaptive scoring, MAP estimation, and international benchmarking frameworks.
- [About](https://eduentry.com/about): Organisation background, assessment approach, and data sources.
- [Try a Sample](https://eduentry.com/demo): Four free sample questions (one per subject) with no account required.
- [Blog](https://eduentry.com/blog): Articles on international academic benchmarks, standardised testing, school admissions, and education systems.

## Subject assessments

- [English Assessment](https://eduentry.com/subjects/english): Comprehension, grammar, spelling, punctuation and vocabulary for ages 6–17.
- [Mathematics Assessment](https://eduentry.com/subjects/maths): Number, algebra, geometry, fractions and data handling benchmarked to PISA numeracy.
- [Verbal Reasoning Assessment](https://eduentry.com/subjects/verbal-reasoning): Analogies, word relationships, sequencing and logic — tested in 11+ and grammar school exams.
- [Non-Verbal Reasoning Assessment](https://eduentry.com/subjects/non-verbal-reasoning): Pattern recognition, matrices, sequences and spatial reasoning.

## Blog — US

- [US Gifted Program Testing Guide](https://eduentry.com/blog/gifted-program-testing-guide): CogAT, WISC-V, NWEA MAP, and OLSAT explained with IQ thresholds by programme type.
- [CogAT Scores Explained](https://eduentry.com/blog/cogat-scores-explained): CogAT Standard Age Score (SAS) explained — percentile and stanine equivalents, gifted program cut-offs (90th percentile ≈ SAS 121), and how the three batteries (Verbal, Quantitative, Nonverbal) compare.
- [WISC-V Scores Explained](https://eduentry.com/blog/wisc-v-scores-explained): WISC-V Full Scale IQ (FSIQ) ranges, the five index scores (VCI, VSI, FRI, WMI, PSI), gifted cut-offs by programme type, and how to interpret a discrepant profile.
- [CogAT vs. NWEA MAP for Gifted Identification](https://eduentry.com/blog/cogat-vs-nwea-map-gifted): What each test measures, why districts use both, score correspondence table, and what to do when results conflict.
- [NWEA MAP Scores Explained](https://eduentry.com/blog/nwea-map-scores-explained): RIT scores, grade-level benchmarks, and gifted identification cut-offs.
- [NWEA MAP Test Prep: What Actually Works](https://eduentry.com/blog/nwea-map-test-prep): Evidence-based MAP prep for Reading and Math K–12. What raises RIT scores (vocabulary depth, Lexile-matched reading, fraction fluency, adaptive practice), what doesn't (grade-level worksheets, test tricks), and a grade-by-grade strategy guide.
- [My Child's MAP Score Went Down: What It Means and What to Do Next](https://eduentry.com/blog/nwea-map-score-dropped): A drop of 1–3 RIT points is within MAP Growth's standard error. A drop of 4+ points in a Fall-to-Spring window warrants investigation. Covers summer slide, measurement error, test-day conditions, skill gaps, and a 12-week recovery plan.
- [How to Improve Your Child's MAP Reading Score](https://eduentry.com/blog/how-to-improve-map-reading-score): Evidence-based MAP Reading strategies by grade — Lexile-matched reading, morphology-based vocabulary, inference (QAR method), and realistic timelines (4–8 RIT points/year at elementary level).
- [How to Improve Your Child's MAP Math Score](https://eduentry.com/blog/how-to-improve-map-math-score): Grade-by-grade MAP Math strategies — the fraction barrier at RIT 205–220, proportional reasoning at RIT 215–225, resources by RIT band, word problem practice, and a 12-week improvement plan.
- [ISEE vs SSAT Private School Guide](https://eduentry.com/blog/isee-ssat-private-school-guide): Structural differences, score reporting, and school-by-school test preferences.
- [How to Prepare for a Gifted Test](https://eduentry.com/blog/how-to-prepare-gifted-test): Evidence-based preparation strategies by test type for US families.

## Score interpretation

### Academic assessment — standardised scale (mean 100, SD 15)

- Below 85: Needs Support (bottom 16%)
- 85–94: Below Average (bottom 25%)
- 95–109: Average (middle 50%)
- 110–119: Above Average (top 25%)
- 120–129: Exceptional (top 9%)
- 130+: Exceptionally High (top 2%)

A score of 115 = 84th percentile. Most English grammar schools outside London require SAS 111–118; London selective schools (Barnet, Sutton) require SAS 121–132.

### Personality assessment — VIA trait scores (scale 1–5)

Each of the 24 character traits is scored 1.0–5.0. Scores reflect how consistently and naturally the child expresses that trait based on responses.

- **Signature Strengths**: top 5 traits — expressed authentically, feel energising rather than effortful
- **Growth Areas**: bottom 3 traits — highest development potential; framed as opportunities, not deficits
- Traits 6–21 sit in the middle range and are included in the full registered profile
- Scores are relative within the individual, not norm-referenced against a population

## Technical notes

Assessment uses 2PL IRT with MAP estimation. Questions calibrated to difficulty and discrimination parameters. Results are indicative, not diagnostic — question content is not empirically normed with large populations.
